literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) derive from the same paper (PMC5494894) and describe a single construct consistently named 'NETO2-HA'. The 'Protein-HA' suffix convention in the literature denotes a C-terminal HA tag. NETO2 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein (EC 23–349, TM 350–368, IC 369–525); its C-terminus (residue 525) is intracellular. A C-terminal HA tag therefore sits on the cytoplasmic face and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. The topology_derived rule (one extracellular terminus, position unknown) cannot be applied here because the naming convention disambiguates the tag to the C-terminus, not the extracellular N-terminus. The paper's stated purpose — investigating subcellular distribution by lentiviral overexpression in hippocampal neurons — is fully consistent with a permeabilized-cell intracellular HA staining approach. No ledger line reports an insertion at or near the mature N-terminus (residue 23) or anywhere in the extracellular domain (23–349). Zero extracellular tag sites are supported.

literature_other_positions.note: The 'NETO2-HA' construct (C-terminal HA by naming convention) places the tag in the intracellular domain (residues 369–525); used for subcellular distribution imaging in permeabilized hippocampal neurons, not a surface-exposed tag.
